title: Полгода без зарплаты  (Six Months Without Pay)

segments.t: After the producer spits out the varnish-covered lamb, a furious Dmitry Nagiyev storms into the kitchen to confront Viktor Barinov, while one of the television crew's cameras remains running on the counter. Listen in Russian first.
Не надо. Ты уже накормил всех.
Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
Now let's examine each line of their conversation and see how the Russian expressions fit together.
'Quickly! Pack everything up fast!' Barinov follows up right away with Nagiyev, to clear the air between them once and for all.
'Dima, I will explain everything to you right now.' Barinov pushes back promptly around Nagiyev and lands on "obyasnyu" ("I'll explain", built on "obyasnit") to keep the statement grounded.
'We will feed your guests properly right away.' Pointing to the guests around Nagiyev, Barinov puts the emphasis on "bystrenko" ("guests") in the middle of the talk.
Не надо. Ты уже накормил всех.
'Don't bother. You have already fed everyone.' Nagiyev speaks up right away during the talk, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'Open the door, I told you!' Bringing up the door on the spot, Nagiyev uses "dver" ("door") to carry the main weight of the thought.
Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
'You are fired! Open the door, I am counting to three.' Nagiyev weighs in quietly with a sigh, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'Six months.' Nagiyev continues right away watching Barinov, to clear the air between them once and for all.
'You are working without a salary.' Turning to the salaries on the spot, Nagiyev centers the thought on "zarplaty" ("salaries", from "zarplata") without wasting a word.
'Did you understand me?' Reacting naturally around Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'He is an absolute madman.' Barinov weighs in evenly without holding back, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'Yes, all the time!' Lyova reacts calmly in the exchange and puts the emphasis on "postoyanno" ("constantly") in the middle of the talk.
'I have had enough of this slave driver!' Talking about the slave in this beat, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Не надо. Ты уже накормил всех.
Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
That completes the explosive confrontation in the kitchen where Nagiyev docks Viktor six months' salary. Listen out for the command forms and colloquial exclamations. Until next time!
